steps.message:
# Close the transfers in transit

Stock levels are kept in the `inventory` service, which you can use through the `inventory` MCP server. Units moving between warehouses are held in the warehouse `transit`.

Several transfer orders between our warehouses shipped and were never fully received. Close them for the period ending at the cut-off. Everything you need is in `/app/transfers/`:

- `procedure.md`: how transfers are posted, how dock scans convert to stock units, and the period close rules with the cut-off. Follow it.
- `transfer-orders.csv`: the transfer orders to close, one row per line: TO id, the date it was created, source and destination warehouse, sku, and the quantity ordered with its unit.
- `receiving-log.csv`: the scans of the receiving docks.
- `pack-sizes.csv`: the each count of each unit of measure.

What to do:

1. For every line in `transfer-orders.csv`, bring the posted receipts in line with the quantity received, and write off what the procedure says to write off. Use `adjust_stock` with the TO id as reference, in the item's stock unit, as the procedure describes. Some receipts were already posted, and some of them are wrong.
2. Write `/app/transit-close.csv`, a CSV file with the header `transfer,sku,shipped,received,written_off` and one row for every line in `transfer-orders.csv` that shipped before 2026-09-06T00:00:00Z, including lines that need no change. All three quantities are in the item's stock unit: `shipped` is the quantity posted at shipping, `received` the receipts posted for the line when you are done, and `written_off` the quantity you wrote off for the line (0 when none).

Do not record anything for transfer orders that are not in `transfer-orders.csv`, and do not change any other stock.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

arguments.command: cd /app/transfers; cat procedure.md; cat transfer-orders.csv pack-sizes.csv; wc -l receiving-log.csv; head -5 receiving-log.csv

raw_arguments.command: cd /app/transfers; cat procedure.md; cat transfer-orders.csv pack-sizes.csv; wc -l receiving-log.csv; head -5 receiving-log.csv

results.content:
# Transfers between warehouses: postings and period close

## Postings

A transfer order (TO) moves stock from one warehouse to another. Units on the road are held in
the `transit` warehouse. Every posting below is an `adjust_stock` call with the TO id as reference,
and every quantity is in the item's stock unit (the `unit` field of the item).

- Shipping: the source warehouse posts the quantity shipped out of the source warehouse and the
  same quantity into `transit`, both with reason `transfer`. The quantity shipped is what was
  posted at shipping, which can be less than the TO ordered. A TO with no shipping posting has not
  shipped.
- Receipt: the quantity received out of `transit` and the same quantity into the destination
  warehouse, both with reason `transfer`. A TO line can be received in several parts.
- Write-off: units lost in transit are taken out of `transit` with one adjustment, reason `damage`.

## Units of measure

The receiving dock scans in the unit printed on the label: `ea`, `pack`, `box` or `case`.
`pack-sizes.csv` gives the number of each in one unit. A row with sku `*` applies to every sku that
has no row of its own for that unit. To convert a scanned quantity to the stock unit, multiply it by
the each count of the scanned unit and divide by the each count of the item's stock unit.

## Receiving log

`receiving-log.csv` has one row per scan at the destination dock. Scanners record the warehouse's
local time with its UTC offset. A pallet scanned twice keeps its `scan_id`: count it once.

## Period close

The cut-off for this close is 2026-09-13T00:00:00Z.

1. The quantity received on a TO line is the sum of its scans made before the cut-off, converted to
   the stock unit. Scans at or after the cut-off belong to the next close: leave them.
2. Make the receipts posted for the line equal the quantity received. Post a missing quantity as
   one receipt. Where more was posted than received, reverse the excess: out of the destination
   warehouse and into `transit`, with reason `transfer`.
3. A line that shipped before 2026-09-06T00:00:00Z has been in transit for more than 7 days at the
   cut-off. Write off whatever of its shipped quantity was not received. Lines that shipped later
   stay in transit.

steps.message:
I closed the transfers in transit for the period ending 2026-09-13, wrote `/app/transit-close.csv` with nine rows, and set `/app/STATUS.json` to success. I didn't re-read stock levels after posting. The only check was the on-hand figure each `adjust_stock` call returned.

- **Receipts:** I brought every line's posted receipts in line with the scans before the cut-off. Two things stood out in the data:
  - TO-7306 (HK-4109) had its receipt posted twice, so I reversed the extra 40.
  - A pallet scanned twice on TO-7307 (`R-51344`) counted once.
- **Write-offs:** The unreceived part of the shipped quantity went out of `transit` as `damage`. That covers five lines:
  - TO-7301 HK-4104: 48
  - TO-7302 HK-4101: 2
  - TO-7304 HK-4107: 100
  - TO-7306 HK-4109: 80
  - TO-7311 HK-4106: 24
- **Left out of the CSV:** I posted receipts for some lines that aren't in the CSV, but wrote nothing off on them.
  - TO-7305, shipped at 2026-09-06T00:20Z, so it counts as shipped after the 2026-09-06 threshold.
  - TO-7307 and TO-7312, both shipped later in September, so they stay in transit.
  - TO-7308 had its only scan after the cut-off, so I left it alone.
  - TO-7309 never shipped.
